title: Proactive on-ramp controller for predictable throughput and cold-start elimination
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated fleets observe variable tail latency during bursty onboarding windows when tenant traffic first arrives. The dominant sources are (1) model weight residency transitions, (2) KV cache coldness for chat-style workloads, and (3) conservative autoscaler ramp due to reactive metrics. This results in missed throughput commitments and manual ops interventions.

Goal: Build a Proactive On-Ramp Controller (PORC) that deterministically stages weights, probes KV working sets, and coordinates a short pre-warm autoscaling path so tenants hit their throughput targets within the SLA window (90s target), without excessive overprovisioning across a fleet.
background: Existing efforts handled warm pools and KV priming via reactive background loaders and ad-hoc heuristics. Recent incidents (see postmortem: DOC-INC-2026-01) show interior jitter when many tenants ramp concurrently. Current warm codepaths lack tenant-priority awareness and do not surface pre-warm progress in Console, which hampers both debugging and billing transparency.
proposal: Implement PORC as an autonomous controller running in the Dedicated control plane with the following capabilities: 1) Tenant intent signal ingestion (API hint / route metadata) to predict imminent traffic. 2) Multi-phase on-ramp plan: weight residency handshake, KV probe sweep (prefix probing + approximate state probes), and a short autoscale step with a guaranteed throughput target. 3) Fleet-awareness to avoid noisy-neighbor storms: cluster-level admission and spread constraints. 4) Observability hooks: per-tenant prewarm timeline, tokenized cost estimate, and success/failure reasons surfaced to Console and the tenant's rollout logs. 5) Safety: automatic rollback to baseline autoscaling if prewarm fails or kernel-level OOMs occur.
tasks: Design PORC control API and schema (control plane protobufs and REST hooks)
Implement tenant intent annotations in route config and SDKs
Weight residency handshake: lightweight RPC to candidate GPU nodes to reserve memory pages
KV probe module: implement staged prefix probes, sample-based hit-rate estimation, and backoff
Autoscaler shim: short-lived aggressive ramp policy + automatic decay to normal scaling after 2 minutes
Fleet admission controller: global booking to avoid concurrent heavy prewarms on same physical racks
Console telemetry: wire prewarm timeline, estimated cost, and success metric into per-route dashboard
E2E tests: synthetic tenant ramps with varying sequence lengths and concurrent tenants
Chaos test: simulate partial prewarm failures and verify fallback behavior
Docs + runbook: operator-runbook and user-facing docs for intent annotation and troubleshooting
milestones: M1 - API and control plane schema review (2026-03-05)
M2 - Weight handshake + KV probe prototype (2026-03-18)
M3 - Autoscaler shim and fleet admission (2026-03-29)
M4 - Console integration and e2e tests (2026-04-05)
M5 - Canary on dedicated customer pool and rollout (2026-04-20)
acceptance_criteria: 90th percentile cold-start latency to reach guaranteed throughput < 90s for synthetic tenant ramps matching customer profiles
No >10% sustained overprovisioning across fleet during controlled canaries (cost guardrails enforced)
Console shows prewarm timeline, resource reservation, and final status for each on-ramp event
Fallback path activates automatically and completes with no customer-visible errors when prewarm encounters OOM or weight fetch failure
Automated e2e tests pass in CI with deterministic seed for KV probe timing
notes: Design trade-off: aggressive prewarm reduces customer-visible latency but raises short-term cost and risk of contention—we limit concurrency with a tenant scoring window and rack spread policy.
KV probing strategy chosen to be sampling-first to avoid full-prefix scans against large embeddings stores; we will iterate if hit rates are insufficient.
Prototype validated locally: weight handshake reduced onboarding time by ~55% for 8B model on A100-like nodes (internal perf-run #perf/2026-03-02).
Coordination with Runtime team needed for a lightweight 'reserve_memory' RPC; proposed API in design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/PORC+Design
Keep the autoscale shim time-bounded to prevent cascade upscales; default ramp window = 2 minutes, configurable per-tenant
risks: Over-eager prewarm may exacerbate tail load if many tenants apply intent simultaneously
KV probe traffic could itself become noisy if naive full-prefix probing is used
Kernel or driver-level failures during weight residency handshake could cause node-level flapping; need conservative retry/backoff
Billing clarity: customers may be surprised by short-term cost spikes unless Console cost estimates are clear
test_plan: Unit: control plane decision logic and concurrency guards
Integration: handshake + KV probe + autoscaler shim in stage environment
Load: concurrent 200-tenant synthetic ramp with mixed model sizes
Chaos: simulate weight fetch timeout, node OOM, and control-plane partition
